summary: The milestone completed 13 experiments in 33.4 minutes, including 2 compute-bound experiments. Measure fresh-source reuse parity and end-to-end cost took 13.38 minutes, while Canary Qwen3.8 source reuse and warm-prefix comparators took 1.99 minutes. The supplied data does not identify why the first compute-bound experiment took longer.
bottlenecks_identified: Measure fresh-source reuse parity and end-to-end cost set the critical path at 13.38 minutes. No phase-level timing is available to explain why it took longest.
Measure persistent-journal latency and durable throughput was the longest synthesis-only entry at 7.5 minutes. This is not a GPU bottleneck, and no stage-level timing is available.
The GPU snapshot is not aligned to compute-task execution windows. It cannot establish compute-task efficiency or identify a missed eligible parallel-model dispatch.
improvements_suggested: Add structured phase timers and restart checkpoints to each experiment. Record setup, model load, inference, validation, and artifact-write time when those phases apply.
Sample GPU utilization during each compute-task window. Join each sample to the task, process, model count, device, and runner choice.
Add readiness-aware device scheduling for independent compute tasks. Reclaim stale model allocations before launch, and use the second GPU when dependencies permit.
Cache validated source-compilation and preparation outputs with explicit validity keys. Reuse them only when the experiment contract permits it.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument task-scoped phase timing and GPU telemetry.
Add readiness-aware scheduling and stale-allocation cleanup across the two GPUs.
Add validated preparation caches and restart checkpoints to the source-reuse workflow.
meta_reflection: Disk-mtime reconstruction establishes duration order but not causal phase costs or task-aligned device use. The 0% savings estimate reflects the absence of a measured counterfactual; it does not claim that the suggested changes have no value.
